facts.text: Munroe Falls was founded in 1838 when brothers William and Edmund Munroe purchased mills and 250 acres, naming the new village after themselves.
The Pennsylvania and Ohio Canal opened on August 4, 1840 just north of the Cuyahoga River, following the path of today’s railroad tracks through Munroe Falls.
The Munroe Falls Historical Society, founded in 1976, runs a 19th‑century home museum that houses local history exhibits and a library.
Munroe Falls Town Hall, originally built in 1885 as a township school, now serves as the village’s civic center.
A stone summer kitchen built around 1817 on a historic home in Munroe Falls is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
